title: Multimodal Streaming Ingestion Pipeline with Backpressure
subtitle: Zero-Copy Byte Buffering, Chunked Audio/Video Tokenization and Queue Throttling
problem_statement: A multimodal ingestion pipeline processes live video, audio, and text streams from 10,000 concurrent IoT cameras. The pipeline experiences Out-Of-Memory crashes and 30-second pipeline lag because upstream WebSocket ingestion buffers payloads in heap memory without backpressure when downstream GPU vision encoders throttle.

faded_bug.description: Unbounded in-memory queue buffers video chunks during GPU encoding spikes, triggering container OOM.

studio_1_runtime.correct_fix_diff:
- inputChan chan []byte
+ // Bounded channel with reactive backpressure and client-side drop policy
+ inputChan make(chan []byte, 100)
+ select { case vp.inputChan <- chunk: default: vp.shedLoadAndNotifyClient() }

invariants.description: Ingest buffer must propagate TCP zero-window backpressure to clients rather than crashing OOM.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Explain how TCP receive window scaling and flow control signal backpressure from server kernel to camera hardware.
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: If a camera ignores TCP backpressure, what load-shedding policy (dropping B-frames vs dropping I-frames) preserves stream coherence?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: How do you handle zero-copy transfer of 4K video frames from Linux network buffers to GPU VRAM via GPUDirect Storage / RDMA?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: Bandwidth ingestion for 10,000 streams consumes 20 Gbps. How do you implement client-side edge motion detection to transmit only delta frames?

counter_probes.counter_question: If incoming network bandwidth is 10Gbps and downstream processing slows to 2Gbps, how many seconds before a 64GB RAM node crashes with OOM?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: Approximately 60 seconds. All queues in highload distributed systems MUST be strictly bounded, with reactive TCP backpressure or explicit load-shedding.
